Pethahiah
peth-ah-HY-ah
proper noun
Hebrew pethachyah, “the LORD hath opened” or “whom the LORD sets free,” the head of the nineteenth priestly course, and a Levite who led in confession.

Biblical Definition

Pethahiah is named as the head of the nineteenth course of the priests in the division which David appointed for the sons of Aaron, that the house of the LORD might be served in order (1Ch 24:16). His name signifies “the LORD hath opened,” a fitting word for one set to minister where the way into the holy place was opened by sacrifice. The same name is borne by a Levite who stood among those that led the great congregation in confession and worship after the return, when the Levites said, Stand up and bless the LORD your God for ever and ever (Neh 9:5), and by a man of the children of Zerah of Judah who was at the king’s hand in all matters concerning the people (Neh 11:24). The dictionary honours that the name, meaning the LORD’s opening, is found both at the altar and in the mouth of those who called Israel to bless their God. The courses of Aaron, opened to their service by lot and by birth, ministered in turn and passed away, hindered by death; but the LORD hath opened by His Son a new and living way into the holiest, which the blood of bulls and goats could never open. Pethahiah stands as a witness that He who opened the priestly courses hath now opened heaven itself, that we may come boldly to the throne of grace through the great High Priest who ever liveth.

Webster 1828 Definition

The head of the nineteenth course of the priests, and the name of a Levite who led in confession after the return.

expand to see more

PETHAHIAH, the head of the nineteenth of the four and twenty courses of the priests appointed by David.

The name signifies “the LORD hath opened” or “whom the LORD sets free.”

A Levite of the same name led the congregation in confession after the return.

A Pethahiah of the children of Zerah was at the king’s hand in matters of the people.

It witnesses to the LORD who openeth the way into His house and His worship.

Key Scripture

1Ch 24:16 — "The nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezekel,"

Neh 9:5 — "Then the Levites, Jeshua, and Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodijah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah, said, Stand up and bless the LORD your God for ever and ever: and blessed be thy glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise."

Heb 10:20 — "By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;"

Heb 7:25 — "Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them."

Modern Corruption

A name of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the LORD who openeth the way into His house and His worship.

expand to see more

Pethahiah is a name of the sacred record, of a priestly course and of a Levite of the confession, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name may know it for a real house and a real man, set by a real God to serve and to lead the people in blessing His name.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the LORD’s opening of the way to Himself. He whose name meant “the LORD hath opened” ministered where sacrifice opened the holy place; but Christ hath opened a new and living way through the veil of His flesh. The saint may remember Pethahiah, and bless the LORD who hath opened heaven and bids us come boldly to the throne of grace.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “the LORD hath opened,” Pethahiah names the nineteenth priestly course and a Levite of the confession.

expand to see more

Pethahiah — Hebrew pethachyah, “the LORD hath opened.”

He was the head of the nineteenth of the four and twenty priestly courses.

A Levite of the same name led the congregation in confession after the return.

He called the people to stand up and bless the LORD for ever.

A Pethahiah of Zerah was at the king’s hand in the people’s matters.

Usage

"Like Pethahiah whose name means the LORD hath opened, the way into God’s house is opened by His own appointment."

"Christ hath consecrated a new and living way through the veil, that we may come boldly to the throne of grace."

"With Pethahiah the Levite we may stand up and bless the LORD our God for ever and ever."
